{{Quote|Imperial Intelligence believes the rebels have established an outpost somewhere in the Horox System.|Darth Vader briefing Sergeant Kreel|<ref name="Star Wars 37">[[Star Wars (2015) 37|''Star Wars'' (2015) 37]]</ref>}}
'''Imperial Intelligence''', also known as '''Military Intelligence''', '''Imperial Military Intelligence''', or the '''Imperial Intelligence Services''', was an espionage organization of the [[Galactic Empire]] that provided services on their own accord and also fed resources to the other [[Imperial Military]] branches, the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military|Joint Chiefs]], and [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. Imperial Intelligence was organized out of five [[Galactic Republic]] intelligence agencies, one of which was [[Republic Intelligence]].

The agency orchestrated the [[Senatorial arrests]] and played a large role in the intelligence gathering during the [[Berch Teller campaign]]. It had oversight of the operations of the [[Naval Intelligence Agency]], which was briefly made a separate organization before being folded back under Imperial Intelligence. MI also had weapons development oversight of the [[Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research]]. [[Director]] [[Orson Callan Krennic]], the leader of the secretive department, was a member of Imperial Intelligence. Whilst a member of MI, Krennic used every tool at his disposal to find [[Galen Walton Erso]] to bring him back into Imperial service.

In [[4 BBY]], [[Tseebo]], an agent of the MI affiliated [[Imperial Information Office]], fled with confidential data. The [[Rodian]] [[Rescue of Tseebo|escaped]] from Lothal into hiding with the help of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell. Later, IIO [[Controller]] [[Boon|LT-319]] and the personnel of his [[IGV-55 surveillance vessel]] embarked on a [[Mission to recover Imperial codes|mission]] to hijack the Spectres' [[C1-series astromech droid]] [[C1-10P|Chopper]] and use him to obtain intelligence on the [[Phoenix Cell]]'s [[Chopper Base|hidden base]]. However, they were defeated by Chopper's rebel allies and the former Imperial [[RA-7 protocol droid]] [[AP-5]].

In roughly [[1 BBY]], a [[DT-F16's squad|squad]] of [[death trooper]]s were tasked with guarding a [[kyber crystal]] being [[transport]]ed aboard a [[Freighter 2716|freighter]] to the [[Tonnis sector]] for [[Project Stardust]]. Death troopers led by Director Krennic executed the [[scientist]]s of the [[kyber crystal research team]] to punish their team leader, Galen Erso, for conspiring with enemies of the Galactic Empire. Furthermore, death troopers participated in the [[Battle of Scarif]] and the [[Battle for Tatooine]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. In around [[1 ABY]], Imperial Intelligence had leads on a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[Horox III rebel outpost|outpost]], which eventually resulted in its destruction by the members of [[Task Force 99]].

==Description==
===Overview===
{{Quote|Success invites scrutiny. Our cousins in Military Intelligence have been salivating over our interrogation results and have convinced the Emperor that Doctor Gorst is too valuable to be a one-man ISB asset. […] I'm counting on you to keep watch on these idiots.|ISB [[Major]] [[Lio Partagaz]] speaks to [[ISB Supervisor]]s [[Lonni Jung]] and [[Avril Heert]], demonstrating the rivalry between the ISB and Imperial Intelligence in the process|<ref name="Festive Evening">{{Andor|What a Festive Evening}}</ref>}}
The [[Galactic Empire]] had carefully divided its intelligence and counterintelligence efforts beneath two different organizations. Information that dealt primarily with military matters fell under Imperial Intelligence, a branch of the [[Imperial Military]]. Meanwhile, information that dealt with potential insurrection and treason fell under the purview of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] (ISB), a branch of [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order|COMPNOR]].<ref name="CaM">''[[Cyphers and Masks]]''</ref> Also identified as its cousin,<ref name="Festive Evening" /> the ISB was a sister agency and rival to Imperial Intelligence over resources, abilities, and areas of responsibility.<ref name="Tarkin" /> In the earliest weeks of the Empire, Imperial Intelligence had found itself busy with ISB-style cases as the other agency was still being established.<ref name="MoF" /> However, the Imperial Security Bureau would grow from a handful of [[agent]]s into an organization double the size of their rival within fourteen [[Standard year|years]].<ref name="AbEverything">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref>

The organization was the direct descendant of the [[Galactic Republic]]'s four competing intelligence agencies<ref name="Dawn" /> and [[Republic Intelligence]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> To prevent corrupt [[senator]]s from using the agencies they preferred, the intelligence heads combined forces around the time the emperor took control. Unified under a group known as the [[Ubiqtorate]], Imperial Intelligence monitored organizations, enemy forces, governments and corporations. Agents generally regarded their COMPNOR counterparts as inefficient and ineffective compared to their own services and the military.<ref name="Dawn" />

They also provided services to the other military branches of the Galactic Empire. In regards to military matters, they focused on issues such as threat reports, analysis, managing assets who were gathered information, and providing briefings to the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military]] and [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. A part of Imperial Intelligence, the [[Naval Intelligence Agency]] was made a separate organization for some time, though it continued to be referred to as "Military Intelligence," before being folded back under Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="Tarkin" />

Imperial Intelligence focused specifically on information directly relevant to military actions and strategic planning. This included traitors within the military and attacks on Imperial facilities or contractors that had housed or supplied the military with necessary resources. The organization was also permitted to investigate leads on suspected military firms that worked against the Galactic Empire. This included [[planet]]ary [[garrison]]s or [[mercenary]] units that had access to military-grade equipment.<ref name="CaM" />

Imperial Intelligence's authority was constrained regarding opposition groups that worked without a military framework. If leads revealed an organization that was essentially a ragtag [[militia]] armed with hunting [[rifle]]s, then that investigation had to be transferred to ISB. Groups that concentrated on civilian targets like [[Foodstuff|food]] depots, [[Factory|factories]] or even government buildings were treated similarly, as were individuals who promoted rebellious beliefs, even in public forums. Any such complications prevented Imperial Intelligence from acting upon its leads. Delays in transferring investigations to ISB often gave suspects opportunities to elude capture, much to the frustration of Imperial agents.<ref name="CaM" />

===Organization===
Imperial Intelligence was composed of a leadership—the [[Ubiqtorate]]—and six main branches: [[Analysis]], [[Adjustments]], the [[Bureau of Operations]], [[Intelligence]], the [[Internal Organization Bureau]], and [[Sector Plexus]]. The Internal Organization Bureau was further made up of [[IntCon]] and [[IntSec]]. Also, the Sector Plexus branch was made up of the [[System Cell]]s.<ref name="Dawn" /> Furthermore, MI had oversight over the [[death trooper]]s, the [[Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research|Advanced Weapons Research]] [[division]],<ref name="UVG" /> the [[Naval Intelligence Agency]],<ref name="Tarkin" /> and the [[Imperial Information Office]].<ref name="Double Agent Droid Ep Guide" />

Imperial [[Intelligence officer|Intelligence]] [[Imperial officer|officers]] wore a white [[Imperial officer's uniform|uniform]] that was similar to the ISB. The uniform was composed of a [[Color|white]] tunic with a [[rank insignia plaque]] and [[code cylinder]]s, black-flared breeches, a black [[utility belt]], black knee-high [[durasteel]]-toed [[leather]] [[boot]]s, and an optional black [[Imperial kepi|command]] [[Hat|cap]] and leather [[glove]]s.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="Officer uniform note">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' states that the non-[[Grand Admiral]] [[Color|white]] [[Imperial officer's uniform|uniform]] was worn by members of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s intelligence community. Since ''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' confirms that Imperial Intelligence were an intelligence agency, they must have worn the white uniform in some capacity.</ref>

===Death troopers===
Death [[trooper]]s, who wore a specialized [[stormtrooper armor]] with a dark gleam, were the elite [[soldier]]s of Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="Death Troopers old">{{Databank|imperial-death-troopers|Imperial Death Troopers|oldversion=20180311114901}}</ref> These soldiers served as bodyguards to high-[[Military rank|ranking]] Imperial officers and were used as elite [[Special forces|special assignment]] [[commando]]s.<ref name="UVG" />

===Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research===
Advanced Weapons Research was an agency responsible for special research and development of classified weapons, both before and during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Weapons development fell under the arm of Imperial Intelligence while the Imperial Security Bureau defended the agency's secrets.<ref name="UVG" />

===Imperial Information Office===
The Imperial Information Office was a government office that was part of Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="Double Agent Droid Ep Guide" /> Some personnel wore [[AJ^6 cyborg construct]]s and [[brain]] [[Cybernetics|implants]] which could connect to [[computer]]s and download information, to increase efficiency.<ref name="Epic Battles">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Visual Guide: Epic Battles]]''</ref> IIO operatives had access to Imperial Intelligence resources such as [[IGV-55 surveillance vessel]]s, which were used to monitor communications and scan data for signs of rebel activity and sedition.<ref name="DB listener ship">{{Databank|imperial-listener-ship|Imperial listener ship}}</ref>

===Naval Intelligence Agency===
The Naval Intelligence Agency was an intelligence agency that served the [[Imperial Navy]]. NavInt was made a separate organization for some time before being folded back under its original parent agency.<ref name="Tarkin" />

==History==
===Origins===
Imperial Intelligence was organized out of five<ref name="Tarkin" /> intelligence agencies following the [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformation]] of the Galactic Republic into the Empire at the [[Mission to Mustafar|end]] of the [[Clone Wars]]<ref name="Dawn" /> in [[19 BBY]].<ref name="SW:GA">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> One of the five founding organizations was Republic Intelligence.<ref name="Tarkin" /> Although their missions differed slightly, there was a rivalry between Intelligence and the Imperial Security Bureau,<ref name="UVG" /> a sub-agency of COMPNOR.<ref name="Tarkin" /> Intelligence agents often derided the Security Bureau's obsession over [[treason]]. A common joke among them was, "How many ISB agents does it take to change a light bulb? Two. One to remove it. Another to accuse the first of disloyalty!"<ref name="AbEverything" />

[[Imperial calendar|One day]] after the formation of the Empire, Imperial Intelligence [[Senatorial arrests|arrested]] 63 senators on charges of conspiracy and treason. These senators were part of the [[Delegation of 2,000]], a group of senators who attempted to limit Palpatine's growing [[Politics|political]] power.<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> A probe droid active under Imperial intelligence surveyed the planet [[Lothal]], which Imperial intelligence recorded the usefulness of.<ref name="197 Probe">{{InsiderCite|197|Probing the Galaxy: Imperial Reconnaissance Report}}</ref> Between [[19 BBY]] and [[18 BBY]],<ref name="18 or 19 Timeline">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates ''[[Adventures in Wild Space: The Steal]]'', during which [[Ryder Azadi]] was the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Governor of the Lothal sector]], to [[18 BBY]]. ''Timelines'' further dates the [[Declaration of a New Order|founding]] of the Empire to [[19 BBY]]. Since the position was established after the [[takeover of Lothal]] according to ''[[Nexus of Power]]'' and ''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'', and must also occur after the Empire was founded, the takeover must have started between those two dates.</ref> the Empire [[Takeover of Lothal|moved onto]] Lothal and began what would become an occupation.<ref name="NOP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> At some point, a probe also surveyed the planet [[Tatooine]].<ref name="197 Probe" />

===Berch Teller's campaign===
Five [[Standard year|years]] later in [[14 BBY]],<ref name="Tarkin date note">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] to [[14 BBY]].</ref> when [[Governor]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin|Tarkin]] and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] [[Mission to Murkhana|visited]] [[Murkhana]] on an investigative mission, former Republic Intelligence officer [[Berch Teller]] and a few of his [[Berch Teller's rebel cell|accomplices]], including [[Anora Fair]], hijacked Tarkin's [[Starship|vessel]], the ''[[Carrion Spike]]''. They [[Death|killed]] the [[Unidentified Carrion Spike captain|ship's captain]] and [[Unidentified Imperial communications officer (Carrion Spike)|comms officer]], along with two [[stormtrooper]]s, before taking off. The Imperials forced a [[Faazah|local]] [[Sugi]] [[crime lord]] to give up his [[Parsec Predator|ship]] to them, and attempted to stop the captured ''Spike''. However, Teller and his crew got away.<ref name="Tarkin" />

After the successful hijacking, the insurgents of the ''Carrion Spike'' went on a [[Berch Teller campaign|campaign]] of destruction against various Imperial targets, such as [[Galidraan Station]]. Imperial Intelligence attempted to track and analyze their activities in order to capture them. The hijackers' information, however, was supplied to them by [[Vice Admiral]] [[Dodd Rancit]], the [[Deputy Director]] of the Naval Intelligence Agency. However, Rancit was revealed as a traitor and executed on Vader's orders. He was replaced by [[Wullf Yularen]], and Naval Intelligence was brought back under Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="Tarkin" />

===The hunt for Galen Erso===
After landing a lofty appointment in Imperial Intelligence, [[Orson Callan Krennic]] used every tool at his disposal to track down [[Galen Walton Erso]].<ref name="UVG" />

===Fighting the Rebellion===
====Rebel encounters====
In [[5 BBY]]<ref name="AndorDate">{{AndorDate|104}}</ref> an agent of Imperial Intelligence managed to take a picture of [[Luthen Rael]],<ref name="Rise">''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''</ref> the spymaster behind [[Axis network]], as he was arriving on [[Ferrix Terminal]].<ref name="Reckoning">{{Andor|Reckoning (episode)}}</ref> Later, during the preparations to lay a trap on [[Anto Kreegyr's group]], ISB [[Major]] [[Lio Partagaz]] requested a meeting with Military Intelligence to discuss [[Spellhaus]], the location of the group's imminent attack.<ref name="Nobody">{{Andor|Nobody's Listening!}}</ref>

On [[Empire Day]] in [[4 BBY]],<ref name="SW:GA" /> the [[Rodian]] Imperial Information Office employee [[Tseebo]] fled into hiding with invaluable data on the new [[TIE series|TIEs]] and [[walker]]s, schedules of [[troop]] movements, tactics, strategies, and a five-year plan for the planet [[Lothal]] and every other world in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Tseebo [[Rescue of Tseebo|escaped]] offworld into hiding with the help of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell.<ref name="Empire Day">{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}}</ref> In [[3 BBY]],<ref name="Timeline">{{AndorDate|206}}</ref> Imperial Intelligence, having been impressed by ISB [[doctor]] [[Gorst]]'s interrogation results, successfully petitioned [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] to allow him to be incorporated into a team shared with the ISB. The [[Imperial Navy]] donated a facility in Coruscant where Gorst was to establish a lab, and ISB Supervisors Jung and Heert were tasked with his protection. The [[Axis network]] was, however, able to infiltrate the facility and murder Gorst before blowing up the building.<ref name="Festive Evening" /> 

In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Double Agent Droid date">''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' seventeen [[Standard year|years]] after the end of the [[Clone Wars]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[19 BBY]]; therefore, the events of ''Steps Into Shadow'' must take place in [[2 BBY]]. According to ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'', [[Maul]]'s final confrontation with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in "[[Twin Suns (episode)|Twin Suns]]" happened thirty years after Kenobi first saw him on [[Tatooine]]. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates that event to [[32 BBY]], "Twin Suns" is set in 2 BBY. "Double Agent Droid" is set between ''Steps Into Shadow'' and "Twin Suns," so the episode must occur in that year.</ref> Imperial [[Controller]] [[Boon|LT-319]] and the crew of his IGV-55 surveillance vessel embarked on an [[Mission to recover Imperial codes|ambitious scheme]] to hijack the Spectres' [[C1-series astromech droid]] [[C1-10P|Chopper]] and use him to obtain intelligence on the [[Phoenix Cell]]'s [[Chopper Base|hidden base]]. However, they were defeated by Chopper's rebel comrades and the former Imperial [[RA-7 protocol droid]] [[AP-5]]. Chopper's master [[Hera Syndulla]] retaliated by transmitting back the data feed to LT-319's ship, creating a data surge that destroyed the vessel and all hands aboard.<ref name="Double Agent Droid">{{Rebels|Double Agent Droid}}</ref>

Afterwards in approximately [[1 BBY]],<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion note">The trivia guide for ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' states that [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] was redesigned to advance the character's age by "18 [[Standard year|years]] or so." As she was last seen was in ''[[The Lawless]]'', which was dated to [[19 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', it can be assumed that the events of ''Heroes of Mandalore'' take place in approximately [[1 BBY]]. As [[In the Name of the Rebellion]] takes place shortly after ''Heroes of Mandalore'', it can be assumed it is also around the [[Standard year|year]] 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]].</ref> a [[DT-F16's squad|squad]] of death troopers led by [[DT-F16]] was tasked with guarding a [[kyber crystal]] being [[transport]]ed aboard [[Freighter 2716]] to the [[Tonnis sector]] for the secret [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[Project Stardust|project]]. Several of DT-F16's troopers were killed by the [[Partisans|Partisan]] leader [[Saw Gerrera]] and the Spectres [[Sabine Wren]] and [[Ezra Bridger]]. DT-F16 survived and took over the defense of the ship. After Gerrera destabilized the [[crystal]], DT-F16 and the ship's stormtroopers tried to flee aboard a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class shuttle]] but the Spectres managed to escape with several liberated civilian [[technician]]s and [[engineer]]s. DT-F16 was killed along with the Imperials aboard [[Freighter]] 2716 and [[Captain]] [[Slavin]]'s [[Slavin's Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer]].<ref name="INTR">{{Rebels|In the Name of the Rebellion}}</ref>

[[File:Acme-LoomingPresence.png|thumb|right|300px|As per the suggestion of Imperial Intelligence, the Star Destroyer ''Dauntless'' was dispatched to Jedha City.]]
During [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[Jedha insurgency|insurrection against the Empire]] on the moon of [[Jedha]],<ref name="197 Probe" /> which was under Imperial occupation to protect a mining operation for [[kyber crystal]]s,<ref name="Rogue One">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> an Imperial intelligence probe droid was dispatched to assess the moon's usefulness for the Empire. The ensuing report concluded Jedha was indeed useful and recommended a single [[Star Destroyer]] be dispatched to quell any rebellion, which was fulfilled when the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Dauntless (Imperial I-class)|Dauntless]]'' was dispatched. However, Gerrera's insurgency continued.<ref name="197 Probe" />

====Galen Erso's defection and Scarif ordeal====
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Rogue One note">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', including [[4D6-J-A7]]'s appearance on [[Scarif]], to [[1 BBY]].</ref> [[4D6-J-A7]] was a [[RA-7 protocol droid]] who served as an [[Administrator|administrative]] [[Aide|assistant]] in Imperial Intelligence and the [[Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="UVG" /> The [[droid]], worked in the [[Imperial Office of Security]]<ref name="Geektionary">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> of the [[Imperial Intelligence and Security Bureau offices]],<ref name="IOoS location note">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' states that [[4D6-J-A7]] was stationed at the Imperial Office of Security on [[Scarif]]. ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' explains that a series of [[Imperial Intelligence and Security Bureau offices]] were located in the [[Citadel Tower]], where the same [[droid]] worked as an [[Administrator|administrative]] [[Aide|assistant]]. Therefore, the Imperial Office of Security must be within the office complex.</ref> which was inside the [[Imperial Center of Military Research|Imperial security complex's]] [[Citadel Tower]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Scarif]]. While there, the [[droid]] was often exposed to classified information.<ref name="UVG" />

4D6-J-A7 was present in the tower when Rebel Alliance agents<ref name="UVG" /> [[Cassian Jeron Andor]], [[Jyn Erso]], and [[K-2SO]] infiltrated the structure disguised as Imperial staff. The Alliance trio passed 4D6-J-A7 within the tower while the droid was conversing with a pair of Imperial officers,<ref name="Rogue One" /> but the droid failed to recognize the infiltrators as a real threat to the Empire.<ref name="Geektionary">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref>

During the same [[time]],<ref name="Rogue One note" /> when the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|first Death Star]] was in its final construction stages, [[Director]] Orson Callan Krennic was accompanied by a [[squad]] of death troopers, who served as his personal [[bodyguard]]. Under Krennic's orders, the death troopers executed the [[kyber crystal research team]] [[scientist]]s as a means to punish Erso for conspiring with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. Later, the troopers fought [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[Alliance Army|ground forces]] and perished during the [[Battle of Scarif]].<ref name="Rogue One" />

===Galactic Civil War===
====Holographic cloaking units====
Sometime in the Imperial Era, ISB Agent [[Andressa Divo]] gave a number of [[holographic cloaking unit]]s that were used by burglars who attempted to steal artifacts from [[Coruscant]]'s [[Galactic Museum|Imperial Museum]] to Imperial Intelligence, whose weapons divisions examined it closely for possible replication. The device was an evolution of the [[Holographic disguise matrix]] that was invented by the [[Snivvian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Sinrich]] and used during the Clone Wars,<ref name="SW:SV:CFGMN">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref> particularly in a [[Plan to kidnap Chancellor Palpatine|botched]] attempt to kidnap [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine<ref name="Crisis on Naboo">{{TCW|Crisis on Naboo}}</ref> in [[20 BBY]].<ref name="SW:GA" />

====Conan Antonio Motti's report====
In a report written by the [[Chief of the Imperial Navy|Chief of the]] [[Imperial Navy]] [[Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti]], after he was [[Force choke]]d by Darth Vader<ref name="An Incident Report">{{StoryCite|story=An Incident Report|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> in [[1 BBY]],<ref name="AIR date">{{FilmDate|IV|1}}</ref> aboard the Death Star, for deriding his religious beliefs in [[the Force]], Motti questioned the [[Chief of the Imperial Army]] [[General]] [[Cassio Tagge]] and Vader's argument about the Rebel Alliance being an immediate threat, due to them possessing the [[Death Star plans]]. In one of his rebuttals, Motti stated that the Galactic Empire had an entire military intelligence unit, whose only role was to assess the trustworthiness of potential threats to the state.<ref name="An Incident Report" />

====Law enforcement intelligence reports====
Imperial Intelligence and the ISB had regularly cut, sifted, and reconstituted law enforcement intelligence reports in efforts to locate potential locations for outposts that belonged to the Rebel Alliance. The military intelligence agencies ordered a collated analysis of suspicious activity reports on a quarterly basis and reverse-mapped it to population research, homing in on cases clustered in [[the galaxy]]'s sparsely populated areas. These were then likelihood-studied by [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] predictors to generate a prioritized list of targets for the surveys of Imperial [[probe droid]]s, that scoured the [[Hyperspace route|spacelanes]] in the years following the [[Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="SW:SV:CFGMN" />

====Anti-Rebel campaigns====
A squad of death troopers fought the Rebel Alliance during the [[Battle for Tatooine]].<ref name="Commander">''[[Star Wars: Commander]]''</ref> [[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra]] claimed to Darth Vader that if Imperial Intelligence had a lead on [[Luke Skywalker]], she bet that [[the Ante]] would have a better one.<ref name="Darth Vader 10">[[Darth Vader (2015) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 10]]</ref>

====Azen Novaren double agent accusation====
In [[0 ABY]],<ref name="IS date">The main story of ''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]'' takes place in the immediate aftermath of the [[Battle of Yavin]], which corresponds to [[0 ABY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''.</ref> while undercover in the [[Staven]]-led [[Dreamers]] at [[Dreamers' encampment|their encampment]], along with [[Inferno Squad]] members [[Iden Versio]], [[Del Meeko]] and [[Gideon Hask]], ISB Agent [[Lar Kantayan]] (who was under the alias of Azen Novaren) was accused of being an Imperial Intelligence double agent, because of a [[homing beacon]] "found" by Meeko and [[Piikow]] aboard the Dreamers' [[Jinata Security]] [[shuttle]]. However, under Iden's orders, Meeko had fabricated the evidence from the logs Azen had recorded over the [[Standard month|months]], while he infiltrated Jinata Security on [[Vardos]]. The accusation resulted in the death of Kantayan, after being [[torture]]d by the Dreamers for seven [[Standard hour|hours]].<ref name="Inferno Squad">''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]''</ref>

====Destruction of a Rebel Alliance outpost====
Around [[1 ABY]],<ref name="SW 37 date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (2015) 37|''Star Wars'' (2015) 37]] to around [[1 ABY]].</ref> Imperial Intelligence believed that the Rebel Alliance had an [[Horox III rebel outpost|outpost]] somewhere in the [[Horox system]]. This turned out to be correct, which eventually resulted in [[Task Force 99]] finding the outpost on [[Horox III]] with the help of local villagers. The force led by [[Sergeant]] [[Kreel]] [[Mission to Horox III|attacked]] the outpost, resulting in the base's destruction.<ref name="Star Wars 37" />

At some point after [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian]] took over [[Cloud City]] on [[Bespin]], an Imperial intelligence probe droid surveyed the city for its uses to the Empire. Another probe surveyed the moon of [[Endor]], which Imperial Intelligence concluded would be a useful place for any secret projects, at one point. At some point, General [[Jay Stobie]] of Imperial Intelligence complied reports on Lothal, Cloud City, Tatooine, Jedha, and Bespin as an [[Imperial Reconnaissance Report]] for use by analysts, who were set to report to Vader.<ref name="197 Probe" />

====Imperial heavy freighter raid====
After a Rebel Alliance [[Raid on an Imperial heavy freighter|raid]] on an [[Imperial heavy freighter]] in [[3 ABY]], from which supplies were stolen to repair the [[hyperdrive]] of the [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Thunderstrike]]'', [[Captain]] [[Tabor Seitaron]], the [[commanding officer]] of the<ref name="Twilight Company">''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]''</ref> [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]]<ref name="Rebel Files" /> ''[[Herald]]'', stated, if there was a base the ''Thunderstrike'' went to, an Imperial Intelligence agent would have already located it.<ref name="Twilight Company" />

====Yrica Quell thoughts on Caern Adan====
In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="AS date">[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']] takes place several [[Standard week|weeks]] after the [[Battle of Endor]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]].</ref> when the [[Alphabet Leader|leader]] of [[Alphabet Squadron]] [[Yrica Quell]] first met [[Balosar (species)|Balosar]] [[New Republic Intelligence]] agent [[Caern Adan]], the [[pilot]] thought if Adan was an agent of Imperial Intelligence, she might have been fearful, although her dread seemed untimely.<ref name="Alphabet Squadron">[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|ISB is a civilian body. Imperial Intelligence is a military body|Pablo Hidalgo, via social media|<ref name="PabloCommentary">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lpnejdixmk2h|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-20|quote=Yep. ISB is a civilian body. Imperial Intelligence is a military body {{C|In response to: "Hey @infinata.bsky.social or @holocronkeeper.bsky.social , quick imperial question sorry to take up time. “Military Intelligence” and “Imperial Intelligence” are the same group right? The cousin/rival of the ISB. Andor got me thinking about it lol"}}|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/fCuoQ}}</ref>}}
[[File:Tarkin_BR.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The novel ''Tarkin'' introduced Imperial Intelligence into canon with the name "Military Intelligence," a name it also sometimes used for the then-independent Naval Intelligence Agency.]]
Imperial Intelligence was introduced into the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] as Military Intelligence through the [[2014]] novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']], which was authored by [[James Luceno]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> The agency's primary name, Imperial Intelligence, was first identified in ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'', which was published by [[Dorling Kindersley]] and first released on [[September 4]], [[2015]],<ref name="AbEverything" /> but the "Military Intelligence" name has also survived as an alternative title.<ref name="Festive Evening" /><ref name="MoF" /> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] outright affirmed in [[2025]] that "Imperial Intelligence" and "Military Intelligence" were the same organization. Hidalgo explained this is thanks to its place in the Imperial hierarchy; Imperial Intelligence is part of the military body of the Imperial state, whereas the ISB technically falls under the civilian structure.<ref name="PabloCommentary" /> In ''Tarkin'', even as the overall Imperial Intelligence branch is called "Military Intelligence," the name "Military Intelligence" is sometimes used to refer to the then-independent Naval Intelligence Agency. By the novel's end, however, the agency is absorbed back into "Military Intelligence."<ref name="Tarkin" /> Factoring in Hidalgo's comments<ref name="PabloCommentary" /> and its usage across ''[[Star Wars]]'' appearances,<ref name="Tarkin" /><ref name="Festive Evening" /><ref name="MoF" /> this article reflects mentions of "Military Intelligence" as mentions of "Imperial Intelligence" with the exception of moments where ''Tarkin'', either as an accident or shorthand, clearly is referring to the then-independent Naval Intelligence Agency with its then-former parent group's alternative name.

The alternative names of Imperial Military Intelligence<ref name="Dawn" /> and Imperial Intelligence Services<ref name="Imperial Troops">{{EncyclopediaCite|Imperial Troops}}</ref> were identified through the [[2018]] sourcebook ''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]''<ref name="Dawn" /> and [[2020]] encyclopedia "[[Imperial Troops]]," respectively.<ref name="Imperial Troops" /> The Military Intelligence name was also used to describe the Ubiqtorate in the [[2024]] book ''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', which suggested "the Ubiqtorate" was the "formal" name of the "Imperial military intelligence" agency.<ref name="Rise" /> However, other sources listed the Ubiqtorate as the agency's leadership.<ref name="Dawn" /><ref name="SWBOOK">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> Hidalgo affirmed this was the case in 2025, describing the Ubiqtorate as "sort of like the command center" for Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="PabloCommentary2">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lpnf5arae22b|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-20|quote=Yeah, the Ubiqtorate is sort of like the command center of Intel. {{C|In response to: "Thank you, Pablo! So, Imperial Military Intelligence falls under the overall military chain of command, whereas the ISB falls into the COMPNOR/civilian side. I’m aware in lore there’s a group called the Ubiqtorate, are they the leaders of military intelligence?"}}|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/Y9kSO}}</ref> [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] also existed in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], introduced through ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', which was published by [[West End Games]] and first released on [[October 1]], [[1987]].<ref name="SW SB">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> Notable [[Director of Imperial Intelligence|directors]] of the agency included [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]],<ref name="X-Wing RS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref> [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Cronal]],<ref name="EP">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref> and [[Ysanne Isard]].<ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>
